what: JBS is the world's largest meat company. It turns cattle, pigs and chickens into beef, pork and poultry at hundreds of plants, and owns brands such as Seara, Swift, Pilgrim's Pride and Primient.
customers: Supermarket chains, food service distributors and restaurant groups on every continent, plus exports to Asia and the Middle East.
money: cattle slaughtered and processed in the United States and Canada
Brazilian and Argentine operations, much of it exported
chicken, in the United States, Mexico and Europe
moat: Scale no rival can match: buying livestock and selling meat in volumes that spread fixed plant costs thinner than anyone else's, with plants close to both herds and ports.
risks: Cattle prices move faster than the prices the company can charge, so margins swing hard
Disease outbreaks or an export ban can close a whole market overnight
Debt of about $21B against thin margins leaves little room when a cycle turns
opportunities: Analysts see roughly 40% upside from current levels, the widest gap among large meat producers
Revenue grew from $72.9B to $86.2B in two years as the company pushed into branded and prepared foods, which earn more than raw meat
The New York listing completed in 2025 opens the shares to index funds and investors who could not buy the Brazilian listing
watch: Cattle prices in the United States and whether the beef margin recovers.
